feature: A level line shows in its layer row thumbnail
summary: A line drawn level or upright now shows its stroke in the layers list, as heavy as a sloped line's, instead of an empty grey tile.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default.

try.do: Pick the Line tool and draw a level line with Shift held.
Look at its row in Layers: a thin stroke runs across the middle of the tile.
Draw a straight up and down line and look at its row.
Switch the Mac to Light appearance and look at both rows again.
Draw a sloped line and an arrow and compare their rows with the level one.

evaluate: Can you tell at a glance that the level line's row is a line?
Does the level line's stroke look as heavy as a sloped line's?
Do sloped lines, arrows and measurements look the same as before?
rough: The stroke in every line thumbnail is about one pixel, because a long line shrunk into a 40 point tile is thin. It now matches sloped lines rather than being drawn heavier.
Level measurements also gained a visible caliper in their rows, a side effect of the same fix.
No mock covers the layer row thumbnail of a line.
